messages.subject: Timer function with amplitude threshold for counting pulses
messages.subject_clean: Timer function with amplitude threshold for counting pulses
messages.body_plain:
Hi there, I have a set of .wavs that I want to calculate numbers of pulses in above a set threshold- I just want to know 'x numbers of pulse' or 'no pulses', for each file.  They are all recorded with the same sensor, and have similar background levels, but different signals within them. I've been playing with the timer function with amplitude threshold for this.

However, the amplitude threshold is calculated as a percentage of the max envelope for each file- the max envelope varies across all my files so the result would be a varied threshold set for each file. There is mention of being able to set the threshold between 0 and 1, but there are no examples of how to scale it in this way.

I would like the amplitude threshold to be the same across all files so that my counts are fair. Am i misinterpeting the documentation on this as a newbie to seewave or am i correct in thinking that i need a workaround to do this?

Many thanks in advance,
Louise

messages.subject: Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.subject_clean: Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am working with 32 bit floating point sound files. Every time I try to apply a frequency filter (ffilter, fir, bwfilter) or down-sample the sound file (resamp), the bit depth of the output wave object automatically becomes 16 bits instead of 32. Can anyone explain to me why this is happening and what I can do to fix it? I don't want to change the bit depth. I only want to filter the sound file and reduce the sampling rate.

Thanks!
Mickey

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mickey,
What you can do is to read the code below so that you replace the default outputw() function.
HTH
Jerome

outputw <- function(
                    wave,
                    f,
                    bit = 32,
                    format
                    )
  {
    if(format == "matrix") {wave <- as.matrix(wave)}
    if(format == "Wave")  {wave <- Wave(left=wave, samp.rate=f, bit=bit)}
    if(format == "audioSample") {wave <- audio::audioSample(wave, rate=f, bits=bit, clip=FALSE)}
    if(format == "ts") {wave <- ts(wave, start=0, end=length(wave)/f, frequency=f)}
    if(format == "sound")  {wave <- phonTools::makesound(sound=wave, fs=f)}
    return(wave)
  }

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] RMS Value "Unit" or Scale
messages.body_plain:
Hello Liam,
The rms() function just computes the root-mean-square of any numeric vector. It has therefore no unit.
If you apply rms() on the envelope, which is not calibrated, you end up indeed with no calibrated data but you can still compare your rms values across different recordings, as soon as the recordings have been done in similar conditions (distance to the source, recording level etc).
HTH
Jerome
